header.summary: Six accredited psychology courses for the RMIT Online Graduate Diploma, refreshed in parallel on one schedule with the ABLE approach, built in Canvas and handed over together.
header.sources: Sources: RMI102 project charter (kick-off deck, 3 September 2026) and Statement of Work 3 (signed 3 September 2026). Reference document.

overview.intro: Curio Group is refreshing six accredited postgraduate psychology courses for RMIT Online. Every course uses the Activity-Based Learning Experience (ABLE) approach, is built in Canvas with LTI integration in RMIT Online visual style, and is tested to WCAG 2.2 AA. Content is developed with an AI-enabled, human-in-the-loop approach, with human judgement at every stage of design, quality assurance and compliance review.
overview.question: How do we refresh six psychology courses in parallel, on one schedule, so the Graduate Diploma reads as a single qualification, and hand over to RMIT Online by no later than 15 December 2026?
overview.note: Each course is a 10-week accredited postgraduate refresh of around 120 learner hours, with three authentic assessments in three rotatable versions (54 assessment artefacts in total).

steps.label: Align
steps.text: kick-off, technical and brand intake, blueprint workshop, then Gateway 1 blueprint review

steps.label: Design
steps.text: weekly storyboard authoring, SME review, remediation, video and graphics, then Gateway 2 detailed design review

steps.label: Build
steps.text: Canvas build, H5P and interactive elements, client environment QA and remediation, then Gateway 3 final sign-off

steps.label: Launch
steps.text: handover to RMIT Online internal teams, and retrospective

steps.label: Retain
steps.text: two weeks of post go-live hot fix and remediation support per course

deliverables: Six courses built in Canvas LMS, in RMIT Online visual style, tested to WCAG 2.2 AA
60 modules of ABLE learning content, with three to five weekly learning activities per module
18 authentic assessments, three per course, each in three rotatable versions with rubrics (54 assessment artefacts)
66 rich media videos, 11 per course, AI-generated with human review and captioned to WCAG 2.2 AA
A readings and industry standards currency report and a scope changes document per course
Full storyboards, a QA report and issue log, and handover documentation with source assets

timing.intro: All six courses are developed in parallel on one schedule. Storyboards arrive one module at a time, three courses reviewed on Wednesday and three on Friday, so no subject matter expert reviews two courses on the same day. These are the contracted stage dates from the signed Statement of Work.
timing.note: The charter records amended working dates: storyboard and SME review 1 October to 23 November, Gateway 2 weekly sign-off 5 October to 30 November, Gateway 3 8 to 22 December and handover 23 December. These are to be confirmed against the Statement of Work end date of 15 December 2026.
timing.criticalPath: RMIT Online provides consolidated feedback within two business days at every gateway. Any delay to gateway approvals compresses the stages that follow and may require the handover date to be renegotiated.

success: All six courses hand over by 15 December 2026 with no renegotiated dates
Every course clears Gateway 3 with WCAG 2.2 AA verified and the Canvas build tested in the RMIT Online environment
One consolidated feedback round and one remediation round per gateway
60 modules, 54 assessment artefacts and 66 captioned videos delivered
The six courses read as one qualification: one blueprint pattern, one asset library and one Canvas template set across the Graduate Diploma
Assessment versions are demonstrably equivalent, evidenced the way agreed at Gateway 1
Readings and industry standards are current at go-live, and the currency report is accepted for every course
RMIT Online internal teams can run and maintain all six courses after handover, and the hot fix window closes with no material defects outstanding
boundaries: Work sits within the existing Course Learning Outcomes. Anything requiring re-accreditation is out of scope
RMIT Online visual style using existing templates and asset libraries. No new brand or template development
Video is AI-generated with human review. Traditional production is quoted separately
Instrument licensing, clinical currency beyond the editions current at build, and Indigenous consultation sit outside the agreed scope
dependencies: Canvas access and LTI credentials at commencement, with the LTI tools named at Gateway 1
Source courses, course maps, Course Guides, CES feedback and the refresh scope documents
Roughly five hours of SME time a week per course through storyboarding, and consolidated feedback within two business days
Existing graphics and visual assets released for reuse, and student delivery start dates advised per course
risks: BESC1516 has no subject matter expert contracted. This is the highest risk in the portfolio
Rachael Grant and Renata Porzig-Drummond each carry two live courses, close to a half-time commitment through storyboarding
Six courses in parallel concentrate the review load. Feedback beyond two business days moves the handover date
Psychometric instrument licensing on BESC1521, and DSM and ICD currency on BESC1520, are unresolved
decisions: Confirm the BESC1516 subject matter expert, Brian Hunt or an alternate
Confirm SME capacity where Rachael Grant and Renata Porzig-Drummond each hold two courses
Name sign-off authorities per course, and agree the Wednesday and Friday review split
